LESSON: SLAVERY AND SERVITUDE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 2.3: Slavery and Servitude
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Slavery and Servitude, part of People and Relationships in Grade 7 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why has slavery and servitude existed for thousands of years?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Slavery and Servitude in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Slavery and Servitude in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. sketch the geographical extent of the regions covered by the Indian Ocean slave trade in Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Slavery and Servitude in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. desire to promote human dignity for a just and peaceful world.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Slavery and Servitude in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society,

   Slavery and Servitude helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade,

   Slavery and Servitude helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. sketch the geographical extent of the regions covered by the Indian Ocean slave trade in Africa,

   Slavery and Servitude helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. desire to promote human dignity for a just and peaceful world.

   Slavery and Servitude helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on the meaning of slavery and servitude and share their findings in class,

2. discuss various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society,

3. use digital or print resources to find out the factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade,

4. draw the geographical extent of the regions covered by the Indian Ocean Slave trade in Africa,

5. develop slogans on ways of promoting human dignity for a just and peaceful world and share in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on the meaning of slavery and servitude and share their findings in class,
2. discuss various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society,
3. use digital or print resources to find out the factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade,
4. draw the geographical extent of the regions covered by the Indian Ocean Slave trade in Africa,
5. develop slogans on ways of promoting human dignity for a just and peaceful world and share in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Slavery and Servitude together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Unity: learners work in groups to brainstorm on various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society.

● Responsibility: learners observe safety precautions as they use print or digital resources to locate the geographical extent of

the regions covered by the Indian Ocean slave trade in Africa.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Human Rights: learners identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African society and locate areas

where slaves were taken during the Indian Ocean slave trade,

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learners use speaking skills as they brainstorm on forms of slavery and servitude.

1. identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society,
2. explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade,
3. sketch the geographical extent of the regions covered by the Indian Ocean slave trade in Africa,
4. desire to promote human dignity for a just and peaceful world.
